title: Zone affinity strategy and edge-cache interplay (working notes)
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures an operationally practical approach to implement 'zone affinity' — a soft, observable binding of tenant requests to a preferred region/zone — while preserving cost and availability benefits of prefix/KV caching and edge caches. The goal is to provide guidance for private + dedicated customers who need high confidence that serving happens within a target region for the vast majority of traffic, and clear, auditable fallback behavior when that can't happen.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Private and Dedicated deployments (VPC/on-prem nodes + dedicated GPU pools). Focus on routing + cache behavior + evidence collection.
- Non-goal: Full legal policy text. This is an operator and engineering playbook, not a contract.

Key constraints and assumptions:
- Customers may require >95% of requests served in-region, but allow controlled fallbacks for burst/DR.
- We operate a global control plane for routing decisions but must not leak customer payload outside pinned region when policy forbids it.
- Edge caches (prefix/KV caches at inference tier) improve cost and latency; naive cache sharing across regions violates strict residency.
- Operators need deterministic, testable rules to demonstrate compliance during audits.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Soft affinity model (sticky with TTL):
   - Each tenant has a configured preferred zone (tenant.zone_affinity = eu-west-1).
   - Requests are routed with soft affinity: initial request picks a zone according to policy (prefers preferred zone), a short affinity token (affinity_id) is issued and cached at proxy level with TTL (default 10 minutes).
   - TTL tradeoffs: longer TTL improves latency/caching but increases risk of stale affinity after explicit customer region change. Default 10min, configurable per-tenant.

2) Affinity enforcement levels (customer-configurable):
   - level=best_effort: prefer preferred zone, allow cross-zone only when no capacity. Produce evidence.
   - level=strict_with_fallback: only allow cross-zone under named emergency codes (DR, capacity_exhaustion), must log and generate evidence bundle for each event.
   - level=hard_strict: deny cross-zone (request fails with 409 and prescribed error msg).

3) Cache scoping and eviction rules:
   - Cache buckets are bound to serving zone + model variant. A cache key includes zone-id when tenant.policy != best_effort.
   - For soft affinity we allow shared caches for short prefixes to benefit cold-starts, but annotate telemetry with cache_sharing=true.
   - Eviction heuristics: when a tenant flips preferred zone, invalidate TTL-bound affinity entries plus all cache entries with tenant-id tag older than X (configurable). Pre-warm new zone cache with small warmup traffic or synthetic requests if allowed.

4) Evidence and audit packaging:
   - For each request served cross-zone under fallback we must produce: request-id, timestamp, originating affinity token, fallback_reason (capacity|zone_outage|operator_override), serving-zone, decision-policy-version.
   - Evidence bundles are signed and retained per customer for configured retention window. Provide a compact CSV and a raw protobuf log.

Operational runbook snippets (for oncall and SRE):
- Operator CLI quick commands:
  - force-affinity-reset: rwdctl tenant reset-affinity --tenant=T123 --zone=us-west-2 --reason=\"migration\",
  - list-cross-zone-events: rwdctl audit list --tenant=T123 --filter=cross_zone --since=24h
- Alarm rules to add:
  - cross_zone_rate > 3% for 10m (non-zero for strict configs) -> P1 alert to infra-residency
  - evidence_bundle_generation_failures -> P1

Telemetry and metrics (minimal set):
- tenant.zone_affinity_ratio: pct of requests served in-preferred-zone (per-tenant, per-hour)
- cross_zone_requests: absolute count (labels: tenant, fallback_reason)
- cache_scope_hits: hits where cache_key included zone-id vs global cache hits
- affinity_token_issuance_rate: to detect churning TTLs
- evidence_bundle_size_and_latency: operator visibility into packaging times

Testing & verification plan:
- Synthetic load tests: create synthetic tenants with affinity set to zone A, simulate capacity exhaustion in A and verify fallbacks respect enforcement level.
- Chaos test: node drain in zone A, ensure evidence bundles recorded and cross_zone_rate remains within customer SLOs.
- Migration rehearsal: scripted boolean migration where we change a tenant's preferred zone and validate cache invalidation + pre-warm behaviors.

Customer migration guidance (for solutions and account teams):
- Recommended migration window: low-traffic window, provide a 24–48h warmup plan.
- Pre-migration checklist for customer: confirm KMS keys availability in target region, share egress consent (if cross-zone fallback allowed), confirm monitoring contacts.
- If customer requires hard_strict: run a preflight that simulates zone failure and verify SLA expectations; discuss cost/capacity implications.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Evidence format: CSV + protobuf vs encrypted JSON? Need legal & compliance input. (See INF-5124)
- TTL default: 10m is a proposal. Ops: do we want 5m for high churn customers?
- Cache pre-warming: is synthetic request pre-warming allowed for regulated customers who block data duplicates? Might need simulated fixtures instead of real data.

Short-term action items (owners):
- (Ethan) Draft RFC for affinity token lifecycle and TTL config — due 2025-11-15 (RFC link placeholder)
- (Priya) Prototype cache key scoping in runtime and measure hit-rate delta — due 2025-12-01 (PR: runtime/edge-cache-proto)
- (Sofia) Wire up telemetry metrics to internal metrics pipeline and create dashboard — due 2026-01-10
- (Lena) Draft evidence schema options and sync with legal — due 2025-11-20 (linked INF-5124)

Notes to self / working concerns:
- Avoid naming this 'pinning' in public-facing docs; 'affinity' sounds more accurate for soft models and less alarming to customers.
- Need to align terminology with product: Console UI will show 'preferred region' but API uses zone_affinity settings. Keep mapping doc.
- Potential perf win: allow global cache for short prefix of tokens for text-generation when strictness is best_effort; need to quantify regression risk for PII leakage.

References & further reading:
- See confluence: zone-affinity-design (linked_artifacts above)
- Related: tenant-pin-migration execution template (internal migration runbook) — avoid duplication, this doc covers runtime + cache interplay rather than migration schedule.

Next sync: schedule review with SRE and product-privacy (30–45m) to resolve evidence format and TTL defaults.
